title: Rejoice in the Lord Always
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Our aim is not just to do and say the right things but to delight in the Lord. Who has more reason to rejoice than the redeemed?
exhortation: Many times in Scripture we are commanded to proclaim the truth of God's word and to proclaim the gospel. We are commanded to hold fast and to stand firm. We are commanded to battle the enemy. But our aim is to rejoice: to delight in the Lord, to have our souls and our hearts so filled with the wonder of Jesus Christ crucified and all he has done for us that our hearts are filled with rejoicing.

If you're like me and have been a Christian for a few years, there is a very real danger of muscling through it. If our aim is only to do as we should and say the words we know are true, but our aim is not delight, not rejoicing in the Lord, we miss the mark.

Trust me, I know that days come when the heart is cold. But that's not something we should be satisfied with or just be okay with. We should say with the psalmist, "Soul, you will again praise the Lord. You will rejoice again. I will rejoice again. My desire is to delight in you, Lord."

For who has more to rejoice about than we, the redeemed? Our Savior went the greatest distance possible to redeem us from a life of sin in which we were dead, with no hope of recovery. There was nothing we could do on our own to bring ourselves to life. Dead men don't do anything. But Jesus breathed life into us, and we can rejoice. Our whole existence in heaven will be knowing and loving and rejoicing in our salvation in Jesus Christ.
prayer: Lord, thank you for sending your Son. Jesus, thank you for coming so that we might know you. You said that whoever has seen you has seen the Father. Thank you for revealing yourself to us, and for revealing the Father to us: so full of steadfast love toward us that you would give up your life to death, even death on a cross.

And yet we also see your holiness, God, unapproachable by unrighteous people like us. But through your death we are made righteous and given access to the Father. Lord, may our hearts be filled with gratitude today for what you've done, and with awe that we can come before a holy God. We pray in Jesus' name. Amen.
